html:
The Osage are a Native American nation of the Great Plains and the Ozarks, today based in Oklahoma. Their name for themselves is Wazhazhe; the map writes it in the Osage alphabet, adopted in 2006.

The Osage speak a Dhegiha Siouan language, like the Ponca, Omaha, Kaw and Quapaw. Their own traditions and their language place their ancestors further east, in the Ohio valley; they moved west, probably in the 1600s, partly under pressure from the Iroquois.

In what is now Missouri, Arkansas, Kansas and Oklahoma they became a great power of the 1700s. They hunted bison, farmed, and traded furs, horses and captives with the French for guns, which they used to dominate their neighbours, among them the Wichita and Caddo.

In the 1800s the United States took most of their land by treaty, and in the 1870s they bought a reservation in Oklahoma. Oil was found under it, and in the 1920s the Osage became rich. That led to the murder of many Osage people for their oil rights, known as the Osage Indian murders.
